requirements.title: NUMERIC_STORAGE_SIZE gives the processor numeric storage unit size
requirements.definition: NUMERIC_STORAGE_SIZE is a default integer scalar constant equal to the size in bits of the numeric storage unit. In a storage association context, 19.5.3.2 p2(1) states that default integer, default real, and default logical nonpointer scalar objects occupy one numeric storage unit, and p2(2) states that double precision real occupies two contiguous numeric storage units.

pending.NUMERIC_STORAGE_SIZE-default-integer-sca: Assign NUMERIC_STORAGE_SIZE to an integer initialized to -777; assert KIND(value)==KIND(0) and RANK(value)==0. Mutate the imported name to CHARACTER_STORAGE_SIZE.
pending.NUMERIC_STORAGE_SIZE-default-numeric-sto: Initialize observed integer sizes to -777; assert STORAGE_SIZE(0)==NUMERIC_STORAGE_SIZE, STORAGE_SIZE(0.0)==NUMERIC_STORAGE_SIZE, and STORAGE_SIZE(.TRUE.)==NUMERIC_STORAGE_SIZE, citing 19.5.3.2 p2(1). Mutate the integer argument 0 to a default character argument.
pending.NUMERIC_STORAGE_SIZE-double-precision-tw: Initialize the observed double-precision size to -777; assert STORAGE_SIZE(0.0D0)==2*NUMERIC_STORAGE_SIZE, citing 19.5.3.2 p2(2). Mutate the multiplier from 2 to 1.
pending.NUMERIC_STORAGE_SIZE-exact-value-process: No portable oracle hard-codes the exact numeric storage unit bit count; future fixtures assert the exact STORAGE_SIZE relations above and positivity only.
